A1.justification: Both PDFs describe IterIS and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. The retained and added material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation, captioning, and NLP experiments in Tables 1–3, with ablations and additional results in Appendices C–D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds evaluated baseline results in Table 2 and Appendix D, Table 14.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and the iterative feature extraction, closed-form updates, regularization, and adaptive weights in Equations (5)–(8) are unchanged. Appendix E adds explanations of existing components.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate DreamBooth/CustomConcept101 composition, SentiCap and FlickrStyle10K captioning, Emotion integration, and seven GLUE tasks. The three GLUE pairs in new Table 14 already appear in Table 13 of v1; the additional caption styles also remain in both appendices.

E2.justification: v2 substantially broadens the evaluated merging strategies by adding task arithmetic, Ties merging, and hyper-linear to the captioning comparison in Table 2. It also evaluates these methods on MRPC/SST2, SST2/QQP, and QQP/MRPC in new Table 14. The existing linear-merging and RegMean comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The reported models, splits, metrics, training settings, and IterIS inference budgets in Section 4 and Appendix B remain unchanged. The 50-sample, six-iteration captioning setting repeated in the new efficiency discussion was already stated in v1. No revised protocol is specified for the added baseline results.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds a worked computational-cost comparison for captioning, reporting 50 × 6 = 300 inner products for IterIS versus 1600 × 1 = 1600 for RegMean. This is an analytical workload estimate, not a new timing measurement. The iteration, regularization, and adaptive-weight ablations in Appendix C remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. The existing averaging over generated images and task combinations is unchanged.

E6.justification: New comparator scores extend the existing findings without changing the original result entries. Table 2 adds CIDEr scores of 0.667, 0.739, and 0.769 for task arithmetic, Ties merging, and hyper-linear, respectively, against the unchanged IterIS score of 0.794. Table 14 adds comparator results for three existing GLUE pairs and repeats the previously reported IterIS scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Equations (1)–(20), assumptions, and Appendix A convergence proof are retained. Changing the encoder layer-count notation from N to J does not change the convergence bound. Appendix E supplies mechanism explanations without revising the formal derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about iterative alignment, sample-efficient merging, adaptive balancing, convergence, and applicability across model families. The added comparisons support those existing claims.

C2.justification: Appendix E newly argues that identity regularization favors a linear-merging solution and that adaptive weights cancel feature-scale effects. It also expands the explanation of computational and memory efficiency. Existing limitations concerning task interference, concept confusion, and humor/romance evaluation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository URL and newly states that all IterIS experiments used a single RTX 3090 and that merging computations run without batching. v1 only referred to a forthcoming code release. Existing implementation and hyperparameter details in Appendix B are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds SHERL and UniPT to the discussion of memory-efficient tuning, plus references for task arithmetic and Ties merging. Hyper-linear uses an already cited work. The overall positioning relative to linear and real-distribution-based merging remains unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized wording corrections, author-order and affiliation updates, a new acknowledgment, and expanded Appendix E prose. The main narrative and section organization remain substantially the same.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains three baseline rows and moves between columns. New Table 14 shifts Figure 11 downward, while the expanded appendix pushes concluding material onto another page. Existing figures and other tables retain their visual content.

improvement.justification: The added comparisons in Tables 2 and 14 strengthen the previously narrower empirical support, while the repository link, hardware disclosure, and component explanations improve reproducibility information and clarity. The gains are limited: the added GLUE comparisons cover only three pairs, baseline tuning details remain unspecified, and the new efficiency evidence is a component-level estimate.
